title: Design a Video Streaming Service
brief: People watch videos on every kind of device, and a small number of creators upload new ones. Watching means fetching many short pieces of the video, which a CDN should serve. Every upload has to be converted into several qualities before it can play, which is slow and heavy, and a new episode of a popular show sends viewers all at once.
constraints: Each video piece must start arriving within 250 ms
About 10,000 piece requests per second at peak, and three times that at a premiere
Pieces are served from a CDN, and storage should see only the misses
Uploads are converted to several qualities in the background, and a burst of uploads must not slow viewers
Recommendations help viewers but are optional

capabilities.label: Serve video pieces
capabilities.hint: Return the next short piece of the video being watched

capabilities.label: Browse and search the catalogue
capabilities.hint: Find videos by title or topic and show their details

capabilities.label: Accept an upload
capabilities.hint: Receive a new video file from a creator and store the original

capabilities.label: Convert uploads to every quality
capabilities.hint: Create the several versions of a video that different devices need. Slow and heavy.

capabilities.label: Recommend what to watch next

scenarios.title: Typical peak
scenarios.description: Steady viewing with the usual trickle of uploads.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Watching and uploading are very different loads. How do you keep a heavy upload from touching viewers?
scenarios.debrief: Viewers fetch pieces from the CDN, and uploads and conversion happen on separate paths.

scenarios.title: A premiere (3x)
scenarios.description: A popular show drops and viewing triples.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Nearly all viewers want the same handful of video pieces at once. What serves them before storage is touched?
scenarios.debrief: The same few pieces are requested by everyone, so the CDN absorbs the surge before storage is involved.

scenarios.title: An upload burst
scenarios.description: Uploads and conversions jump tenfold for a while.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Creators upload a mountain of video. Where does the conversion work wait, and how do viewers stay unaffected?
scenarios.debrief: Conversion work waits in the queue and the transcode workers autoscale. Playback is a different path.

scenarios.title: Recommendations hang
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Recommendations hang. Should playing a video wait for them?
scenarios.debrief: Playback does not call the recommender, and the breaker keeps the rest of the page from waiting on it.

requirements.text: Video pieces start within the latency target at peak
Pieces are served through a CDN in front of storage
Something converts uploads, away from viewers
An upload burst does not disturb viewers
A hung recommender cannot slow playback
The design explains how a video is split into pieces and qualities

rubric: Video is split into short pieces in several qualities, stored as objects, and served through a CDN so storage sees only misses.
Uploads go to storage first; a queue drives workers that convert them, so conversion never competes with playback.
Playback, catalogue and recommendations are separate paths; an optional service cannot slow playback.
Conversion capacity scales out under an upload burst without paying for it all month.
Popular pieces (a premiere) are served from CDN edges; the origin sees a small fraction of requests.

reference.summary: Serve video pieces from a CDN, keep catalogue, uploads and recommendations on their own paths, and transcode behind a queue.
design: User, then a CDN (95% hit), then a Load Balancer that routes by request class: a Playback Service reading Blob Storage; a Catalogue Service over a Search Index and Database; a Recommendation Service behind a breaker; an Upload Service writing Blob Storage.
Uploads continue to a Queue asynchronously, read by Transcode Workers (autoscale to 120) that write the converted versions to Blob Storage.
tradeoffs: A CDN serves nearly every piece, so storage sees misses only. Its cost is small next to the origin it replaces.
Transcoding behind a queue costs a queue and workers, but a burst of uploads never touches viewers.
